w10_P4_001598: The dispatch log at a warehouse records, for each run, a billing figure equal to 12 times that run's adjusted energy total in kilojoules. The adjusted total is the kinetic energy of the loaded trolley expressed in kilojoules, plus a fixed 12 kJ allowance booked to the hoist. The trolley and its load together have a mass of 55 kg, and the trolley rolls along a level rail at a steady speed. The rail controller reports that the trolley's speed in metres per second is a value whose square, less 7 times that speed, plus 6, comes to exactly 0. Two speeds fit that description, and the trolley was running at the larger one. What billing figure does the dispatch log record for this run, in kJ?
w10_P4_001603: A test rig at a parts plant holds 49 steel washers and 86 brass washers, and the loader groups them into identical bundles using the largest bundle size that divides both counts exactly. The rig's control board then sets the sled's acceleration, in metres per second squared, to 4 times that bundle size. The sled itself has a mass of 197000 g and runs along a track 12 m long. The push the drive must supply is doubled when a second identical sled is coupled behind the first, and the plant runs 10 such coupled pairs at the same time. What total push must the plant's drives supply altogether, in kN?
w10_P4_001606: A vibration bench drives a fixture whose acceleration, in metres per second squared, is set to twice the sum of its two dial readings, and both dials are turned to 8. The fixture on the bench has a mass of 24000 g, and a warning lamp on the bench is rated at 15 W. A second identical fixture is mounted on the opposite arm, so the drive must supply twice the push it supplied for one fixture. Expressed in kilonewtons, that combined push is doubled again when the bench is switched to its high-range mode. The bench's calibration report then subtracts a fixed 29 kN offset from the high-range figure. What number does the calibration report give, in kN?
w10_P4_001616: On a laboratory bench a cart carrying instruments has a total mass of 56 kg and is released along a level air track 3 m long. A sensor reports that the cart's speed in metres per second is a value whose square, less 9 times that speed, plus 14, equals exactly 0, and of the two values that fit, the cart was travelling at the smaller one. The bench's log sheet takes the cart's kinetic energy in kilojoules, subtracts a 14 kJ baseline drawn by the track's blower, and then adds back 2 kJ credited to the sensor supply. The final entry on the log sheet is 11 times that adjusted figure. What is the final log entry, in kJ?
w10_P4_001619: A drop-hammer test cell launches a sled whose speed, in metres per second, is 3 times the sum of its two gate readings, and both gates read 3. The sled has a mass of 38000 g, and the cell's warning beacon draws 40 W. The cell fires 12 identical sleds in a batch, so the batch carries 12 times the energy of one sled. From the batch total the operator subtracts 1 J lost in the release latch, and then doubles what remains, because the rig runs a mirrored second bay firing the same batch. How much energy does the doubled figure represent, in kJ?
w10_P4_001626: An audit sheet for a launch rig reports a net energy figure found by taking the rig's total launch energy in kilojoules and subtracting a fixed 16 kJ charged to the control cabinet. The total launch energy is 9 times the energy of a single launch, because the rig fires 9 carriages in each cycle. Each carriage has a mass of 17000 g and leaves the rail at a speed, in metres per second, equal to 7 times a number x. That number x satisfies the condition that x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 14, is exactly 0, and the rig is set to the larger of the two values that fit. What net energy figure does the audit sheet report, in kJ?
w10_P4_001629: A workshop tests an electric winch that accelerates a sled of mass 82000 g along a level floor. The controller sets the sled's acceleration in metres per second squared to a value whose square, minus 6 times the value, plus 5, is exactly 0, and the workshop uses the larger of the two values that satisfy this. The winch has 5 identical drums pulling in parallel, so the total pull is 5 times the pull on the single sled, expressed in kilonewtons. The safety report then subtracts 2 kN for the anchor allowance and a further 5 kN for the floor-bolt allowance. What figure does the safety report end with, in kN?
w10_P4_001633: A ride's maintenance sheet ends with a figure equal to 5 times the energy budget of a single dispatch. That budget is the kinetic energy of the loaded car plus 16 J allowed for the latch solenoid. The car and its rider together have a mass of 28000 g, and the car leaves the top of the lift at a speed, in metres per second, equal to 2 times a number x with 3 then subtracted. The number x is one of the two values whose square, minus 8 times x, plus 12, comes to exactly 0, and the sheet uses the larger of them. The lift chain is 40 m long. What figure does the maintenance sheet end with, in J?
w10_P4_001634: A structures lab closes its report with a value obtained by taking 12 times an intermediate margin and then subtracting a further 16 kN for the reaction frame. The intermediate margin is the force driving the test mass, expressed in kilonewtons, minus 16 kN allowed for the fixture's own weight. The test mass is 104000 g, and it is accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, of 7 times the sum of the two ramp settings, which read 4 and 5. The lab repeats this closing calculation after every rebuild of the rig. What value does the lab's report close with, in kN?
w10_P4_001636: A test loop's report ends with a number found by taking a certain kilojoule figure, subtracting 16 and then adding 8. That kilojoule figure is the kinetic energy of a 48 kg trolley on the loop, expressed in kilojoules. The trolley's speed in metres per second equals a certain accumulated meter total, minus 18. That accumulated total is what the loop's meter registers between the 3rd and the 4th second of a run, while the instantaneous rate it registers at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 2 times t. What number does the report end with, in kJ?
w10_P4_001637: A conveyor audit finishes by multiplying a certain energy balance by 9. That balance is the kinetic energy of the shuttle expressed in kilojoules, less 27 kJ charged to the drive cabinet and a further 26 kJ charged to the chiller. The shuttle has a mass of 30 kg. Its distance travelled along the rail, in metres, is 5 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds minus 2 times the square of that time, and the audit uses how fast the shuttle is moving at the instant 1 second after release. What figure does the audit finish with, in kJ?
w10_P4_001642: A packing line handles 139 tins on one belt and 140 tins on the other, and the supervisor forms identical trays using the largest tray size that divides both counts exactly. The line's test puck has a mass of 36000 g and travels at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that tray size. The line runs 10 pucks per lane, there are 5 lanes on the floor, and the plant operates 6 identical floors. A status lamp on each floor draws 18 W. How much kinetic energy do all the pucks in the plant carry at once, in kJ?
w10_P4_001653: A depot ships 250 crates of one kind and 234 of another, and the loader stacks them into identical columns using the largest column height that divides both totals exactly. A test cart is then sent down the ramp at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that column height plus 27. The cart has a mass of 41000 g, and the ramp is lit by a 60 W lamp. The energy audit takes the cart's kinetic energy in kilojoules, subtracts 23 kJ booked to the hoist and then a further 6 kJ booked to the door motor. What does the energy audit report, in kJ?
w10_P4_001654: A bicycle workshop receives 395 spokes of one gauge and 253 of another, and it bundles them into identical packs using the largest pack size that divides both counts exactly. The workshop's test dummy has a mass of 77000 g and is pushed along the rig at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pack size. Two such dummies are pushed together on one rig, so the rig's drive supplies twice the force needed for one. The logged figure then subtracts 22 N for the trolley bearings, and the workshop runs 10 identical rigs side by side. What total force do the 10 rigs log, in N?
w10_P4_001655: A crane test ends with a reading equal to 4 times a corrected force, because four identical hoists share the same duty. The corrected force is the force acting on the test block, reduced by 18 N for sheave friction and then increased by 1 N for the load-cell offset. The block has a mass of 54 kg. Its upward speed, in metres per second, is 1 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds minus 2 times the square of that time, and the test is read at the instant 2 seconds into the lift, using how fast that speed is changing at that moment. What reading does the crane test end with, in N?
w10_P4_001656: At a ski-lift maintenance shed a test slug of mass 29000 g is fired along a rail. Its launch speed, in metres per second, is 4 times the sum of the two pressure-dial settings, which read 2 and 9. The shed fires 6 slugs in each cycle, so a cycle carries 6 times the energy of a single slug. A pilot light in the shed draws 25 W. The shed also runs a mirrored bay that fires an identical cycle at the same moment, doubling the energy released. How much energy does the pair of cycles carry, in kJ?
w10_P4_001657: A demolition contractor's estimate is 8 times the energy of one district's programme, and each district runs 3 identical sites. A site's programme is the energy of a single swing plus 6 J for the release gear, expressed in kilojoules. The wrecking ball has a mass of 52000 g. Its speed at the bottom of the swing, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the 13 anchor points on the frame, taking 2 at a time. What is the contractor's estimate, in kJ?
w10_P4_001667: A water-jet cutting bay meters its feed pump through a run, and at time t seconds the pump's instantaneous rate is 4 times t squared plus 4 times t. The bay's carriage is launched at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to the total the meter accumulates between t equal to 1 and t equal to 2. The carriage has a mass of 43000 g. The bay fires 4 identical carriages in a burst, and the log then subtracts 18 J for the trigger circuit. How much energy does the log record for the burst, in kJ?
w10_P4_001671: A press shop's daily total is 5 times the force developed by a single line, and each line runs two identical presses, so a line develops twice the force of one press. On the trial curve a press ram's position, in metres, is 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 6 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the engineers read how fast the ram's velocity is changing at the instant 1 second in. In the production machine the ram is geared to accelerate 5 times as hard as that trial figure, and the ram has a mass of 73 kg. The shop's air compressor is rated at 30 kW. What is the press shop's daily total, in N?
w10_P4_001672: A rally team's energy sheet ends by adding 30 J for the starter motor and then subtracting 18 J for the telemetry unit. Before those two adjustments the sheet holds 6 times the kinetic energy of one test sled, because six sleds run the course together. Each sled has a mass of 57 kg, and the course is 250 m long. A sled's speed, in metres per second, is 7 times the largest whole number that divides both 75 and 91 exactly. What figure does the energy sheet end with, in J?
w10_P4_001673: A theme park's annual figure is 9 times the energy booked to one ride, and each ride dispatches 8 identical cars in a cycle. For one car the booked energy is its kinetic energy plus 9 J charged to the lap-bar release, expressed in kilojoules. A loaded car has a mass of 48 kg, and the station platform is 12 m long. The car's speed at the bottom of the drop, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, comes to exactly 0. What is the theme park's annual figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001676: A pile-driving rig logs its hammer's acceleration, in metres per second squared, as the total accumulated between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a stroke, where the instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 4 times t. The hammer has a mass of 135000 g. The rig's guide mast stands 18 m tall. Eight identical hammers fall together on one frame, so the frame carries 8 times the force of a single hammer, and the contractor operates 5 such frames at once. What total force do the 5 frames carry, in kN?
w10_P4_001683: A cable-car depot's final entry is the force on the carriage plus 24 N for the door strut, written in kilonewtons. The carriage has a mass of 188 kg, and the haul rope is 900 m long. The carriage's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by taking a certain number x, subtracting 7, and then adding 8. That number x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 11 times x, plus 28, equals exactly 0. What is the depot's final entry, in kN?
w10_P4_001690: A robotics lab reports 9 times a single arm's corrected thrust, because nine arms work the same cell. The corrected thrust for one arm is the force on its payload, plus 2 N for the gripper spring and a further 26 N for the wrist damper. The payload has a mass of 12000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 2 more than a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values satisfying x squared minus 7 times x plus 10 equals 0. What does the lab report, in N?
w10_P4_001693: A quarry's shaker deck drives a screen assembly of mass 153000 g. The deck's drive is set so that the assembly's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 6 times a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 14, equals exactly 0. Eight identical decks are bolted to the same steel frame and all run in phase, so the frame takes 8 times the force of one deck. The maintenance log then subtracts 1 N to account for the calibration offset of the load pin. What figure goes in the maintenance log, in N?
